text.tspan: Tool platform: sources, persistent catalog, dynamic loading
ToolRuntime registry: handlers re-attached at every start
validation, timeouts, idempotency, approval by risk
source, spec hash, risk, trust, enabled (switch), available
+ loaded tools (appended, saved on the run)
MCP tools are named server__tool, ask for approval unless read_only, and see only the env vars named in env. Egress allowlists apply to HTTP, web search, and MCP.

g.text: Step 1 of 13 · Python tools
A module function registers ToolSpec + handler pairs under its source name.
Step 2 of 13 · Registered
Every source's tools go into the runtime registry.
Step 3 of 13 · HTTP tools
Declarative JSON APIs: GET sends a query string, other methods a JSON body.
Step 4 of 13 · Web search
Built-in Tavily search; the key comes from an env var or a secret file.
Step 5 of 13 · MCP servers
Configured by command (stdio) or URL (HTTP); names become server__tool.
Step 6 of 13 · JSON-RPC
initialize, tools/list (all pages), tools/call. Servers start on first use.
Step 7 of 13 · Cached until sync
Until tools sync reaches the server, its tools come from the last catalog sync.
Step 8 of 13 · Persistent catalog
Spec hashes, risk, trust, the operator's switch, and whether the source still provides it.
Step 9 of 13 · Operator switches
tools disable NAME hides a tool; the switch survives restarts.
Step 10 of 13 · What the model sees
Only enabled and available tools are offered.
Step 11 of 13 · All tools
The default: every enabled tool is in every request.
Step 12 of 13 · Dynamic loading
For hundreds of tools: search_tools, then load_tools; loaded tools stay for the run.
Step 13 of 13 · Untrusted output
Results from web, HTTP, and MCP tools are wrapped as data (prompt-injection defence).
